item.title: C.F.T.C. Officials Considered Investigating Trump’s Memecoin, Then Punted
item.description: Lawyers at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission looked into possible fraud soon after the digital token’s launch, then decided they would not get the commission’s support.
item.dc:creator: Sharon LaFraniere
item.media:credit: Jason Andrew for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission in Washington. The C.F.T.C. is charged with overseeing cryptocurrency and prediction markets, two business sectors in which the Trump family is deeply invested.

item.title: Texas Execution Took an Hour as Prisoner Moaned in Pain, Witnesses Say
item.description: Prison personnel placed needles in the neck and foot of Reinaldo Dennes, who was convicted of killing a diamond broker 30 years ago.
item.dc:creator: Jacey Fortin
item.media:description: The state of Texas execution chamber in Huntsville, Texas, as seen in 2008.

item.title: 2 Earthquakes Strike Los Angeles Area and Central California
item.description: A 5.0-magnitude quake struck around Pinnacles, Calif., southeast of San Francisco. A few hours later, a 4.2-magnitude quake hit just outside of Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe

item.title: Ron DeSantis Ponders a Presidential Run in a Post-Trump World
item.description: In a wide-ranging interview, the governor of Florida talked about the potential timing of a presidential run. “I haven’t made any decisions,” he said.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:description: Gov. Ron DeSantis of Florida said he thinks the 2028 Republican presidential field is likely to crystallize more slowly than in the past.

item.title: A Dairy Farmer Ran for Office to Prove a Point. He Accidentally Won.
item.description: An Arkansas Democrat’s victory in a race for county assessor was one of many unlikely down-ballot wins that showed the depth of the blue wave.
item.dc:creator: Reis Thebault
item.media:credit: Terra Fondriest for The New York Times
item.media:description: Nathan Miller with his dairy cows on his farm outside Fayetteville, Ark.

item.title: New Ph.D. Enrollment in the Sciences Dropped 10 Percent Under Trump
item.description: Falling international enrollment drove most of the decline, but there were also fewer American students starting doctoral programs in 2025.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Adelson, Katrina Miller and Arfa Momin
item.category: American Assn for the Advancement of Science

item.title: Justice Department Gives Up on Alaska Senate Lawsuit
item.description: The Trump administration had sought to block certification of election results if Senator Dan Sullivan, a Republican, lost narrowly in his bid for re-election. Critics had called the suit meritless.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Attorney General Todd Blanche in June. The Justice Department had sued Alaska at the president’s direction over the presence of two candidates named Dan Sullivan in the race for a Senate seat in the state.

item.title: California Thieves Carried Out String of Train Heists, Prosecutors Say
item.description: A crew of 14 men boarded moving trains in Southern California, forced them to stop and made away with sneakers, electronics and power tools, according to an indictment unsealed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Tim Arango
item.media:credit: Alex Welsh for The New York Times
item.media:description: In recent years, trains, especially in the Los Angeles area, have been targeted by thieves with greater frequency, and law enforcement has devoted more resources to countering the crimes.

item.title: Technology Promised Ease. Outages Are Making Many Americans Uneasy.
item.description: Rather than feeling empowered by the digital tools they have come to rely on, many Americans are now questioning how powerless they may have actually become.
item.dc:creator: Campbell Robertson and Elizabeth Dias
item.media:description: Travelers looked at a flight information board full of canceled and delayed flights at San Francisco International Airport after a nationwide ground stop.

item.title: Top White House Cybersecurity Official Is Replaced
item.description: The departure of Sean Cairncross comes after a series of technological outages affected U.S. companies and federal agencies in the past week.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron and Dustin Volz
item.media:description: Sean Cairncross in Menlo Park, Calif., earlier this week.

item.title: Elon Musk Backs Away From MAGA and the Trump Presidency He Shaped
item.description: The man who helped elect President Trump in 2024 and led DOGE is trying to rewrite history.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood

item.title: Agriculture Secretary’s Christian Messages to Staff Went ‘Too Far,’ Judge Says
item.description: A federal judge ordered limits on Brooke Rollins’s promotion of her religious beliefs, saying her emails to her department had violated the First Amendment.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:credit: Shelby Tauber for The New York Times
item.media:description: Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins celebrated “our savior Jesus Christ, who came to free us from our sins and open the door to eternal life,” in a Christmas email to staff.

item.title: Former Biden Chief, With Help From Alex Soros, Will Gather Aides of 2028 Hopefuls
item.description: Jen O’Malley Dillon, who led the former president’s last two White House bids, is inviting top Democratic operatives to a gathering funded in part by the megadonor Alex Soros.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein and Tyler Pager
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jen O’Malley Dillon was the campaign manager for Joseph R. Biden Jr.’s 2020 bid and became the top official on the 2024 campaign for Mr. Biden and then for Vice President Kamala Harris.

item.title: Fiona the Hippo, Star of Cincinnati Zoo and Beyond, Dies After Eating Child’s Hat
item.description: The beloved Nile hippopotamus became ill after eating a children’s hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure.
item.dc:creator: Remy Tumin
item.media:description: Fiona passed away after swallowing a hat that had fallen in her enclosure.

item.title: Fire at Railroad Tie Plant in Alabama Closes Schools and Prompts Evacuations
item.description: The authorities in Attalla ordered residents within a mile radius to leave because of the fire at the Omaha Track, a railroad tie recycling facility.
item.dc:creator: Christine Hauser
item.media:description: A fire was burning at an Omaha Track railroad tie facility in Attalla, Ala., on Thursday.

item.title: Whatever You Thought Texas Was, It’s Bigger and Bluer Than That
item.description: After Democrats broke a decades-long Republican winning streak this month, Texans are reflecting on who gets to define the place they call home.
item.dc:creator: Sasha von Oldershausen and Jesus Jiménez
item.media:credit: Jordan Vonderhaar for The New York Times
item.media:description: The dome of the Texas Capitol in Austin.

item.title: Senate Republicans Block Bid to Rein in Trump on Iran War
item.description: In the first vote on the conflict since the midterm elections, most in the G.O.P. banded together against placing any limits on a conflict that voters repudiated at the polls.

item.title: The Secret History of a 1972 Case on Press Freedom
item.description: An F.B.I. campaign against the Black Panthers and a justice’s questionable failure to recuse himself dealt a blow to protections for confidential sources.
item.dc:creator: Adam Liptak
item.media:description: Earl Caldwell in 1969.

item.title: At Summit With Xi and Putin, Trump Seeks to Project Power Abroad While Sharing It at Home
item.description: Weakened by the midterm elections, President Trump offered hugs, arm pats and smiles to autocrats from Russia and China in contrast to the threats he is making to ascendant Democrats in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.media:description: A trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday offered a welcome respite to President Trump, who has long expressed admiration for authoritarian leaders like President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia and President Xi Jinping of China.

item.title: Senator Warns Congress to Secure Data From Intrusion by Trump Administration
item.description: Gaps in protections for lawmaker communications loom larger as the administration amplifies its threats to criminally investigate Democrats for aggressive oversight efforts.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Savage
item.category: House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack
item.media:description: As Democrats vow to investigate President Trump and his inner circle, the administration has threatened criminal investigations in retaliation for oversight it deems unduly aggressive.

item.title: Los Angeles Prosecutor to Oversee Inquiry Into Search of Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Residence
item.description: The appointment of Bill Essayli to run a key aspect of the so-called grand conspiracy case was the latest shake-up in a central part of President Trump’s retribution campaign.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.category: Federal Criminal Case Against Trump (Documents Case)
item.media:credit: David Crane/Los Angeles Daily News, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Bill Essayli will focus narrowly on the question of whether agents and prosecutors broke the law four years ago when they searched Mar-a-Lago.
